newsitem.title: CHINA: China forex reserves $100.45 bln at Nov -Xinhua.
newsitem.headline: China forex reserves $100.45 bln at Nov -Xinhua.

text.p: China's foreign exchange reserves reached $100.45 billion on November 12, the official Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
The news agency was quoting figures from the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
State media last week reported that the foreign exchange reserves stood at $98.8 billion at the end of October, but officials had long predicted they would top $100 billion before the end of 1996.

Xinhua said the rising reserves reflected a growing trade surplus and an improvement in the balance of payments. It also linked the rise to government efforts to rein in inflation and keep a tight grip on official spending.

China is expected to enjoy an $18 billion trade surplus for 1996, up from $16.69 billion in 1995, the official Securities Daily said on Friday. Other forecasts for this year's trade surplus have been even higher.
